attrs.evidence: The DUAL of the proposal GPT-5.6 rejected, and the reason it is worth having: disjointness cannot establish independence, but a SHARED CAUSE refutes it outright. Two instruments whose declared origins and assumptions intersect are not independent readings, whatever else is true, so the closure only ever bounds independence downward. Over all 21 pairs the intersection is never empty and the floor is ASM-SUBSTRATE-INTEGRITY: every gate in this tree is one Node process reading one filesystem. This is the ceiling on how independent any two results here could be, and it is a small number.
attrs.gap: DEMOTED AT R6.1. The enumeration is sound and the proposition it was attached to is not the one the enumeration establishes. `cause closure` was the overclaim: the sets intersected are DECLARED REFERENCES — origins, assumptions, common-cause notes — and two gates citing ASM-SUBSTRATE-INTEGRITY have declared a dependency on one proposition, not been shown to fail together. Common-cause structure and probabilistic dependence are distinct notions in the reliability literature, and a shared assumption reference is upstream of both. EVID-DECLARED-OVERLAP states what the enumeration proves. Promoting this record again needs a causal argument that the shared references name shared FAILURE MODES, which nothing in this tree has.
attrs.note: The exact species this artifact has caught at four other layers, committed by the round that caught the previous one: a registry relationship consumed above its strength. R6 rejected Fable's `disjoint ids ⇒ independent` and then wrote `overlapping ids ⇒ not independent` in the same section. The sign was flipped and the error was identical.
